newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 gives up early gain as index futures dive on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 gives up early gain as index futures dive on profit-taking.

text.p: The FTSE 100 retreated from a new record high midmorning on Thursday as profit-taking hit index futures following Wednesday's strong rise, dealers said.
"We've seen a massive squeeze in the futures and people are getting the idea now that we've seen the top in the short-term," said a dealer.

The September contract traded at 5,020, 29 points lower, at 0935 GMT having hit a low of 5,011 and an early high of 5,074. Dealers said volume was boosted by a large cross trade with an underlying value of 287 million stg.
The FTSE 100 was 13.3 points off at 5,012.9
Volume in the cash market was a modest 245.8 million.
Trading was nervous ahead of the Bank of England's decision, due at 1100 GMT, on whether interest rates will rise, dealers said.
The market has factored into prices a quarter-point rise which would take rates to 7.0 percent and softer long-term perceptions on interest rates are keeping market sentiment buoyant.
Strategists said forecasts that rates would be at eight percent by the year end now look too high.
"Near term we're looking pretty clever with a softer rate outlook, good results and we're not overbought," said one.
While the market awaited the Bank of England's decision, attention was firmly fixed on corporate results with a raft of FTSE 100 companies reporting half-year figures.
Barclays added 6.5 points to the FTSE 100, putting on 77p to 1,404-1/2p, after strong results and news of a bigger share buy-back.
Shell, however, took 15.5 points off the index after profits fell short of expectations. The stock fell 27p, or 5.7 percent, to 446p.
Disappointing results took Rank and Reed sharply lower. Rank lost 27p to 343-1/2p and Reed 35p to 595p.
Zeneca fell 19-1/2p to 2,027 despite stronger-than- expected profits after the group said launch costs would affect margins in the second half.
Royal & Sun bucked the downward trend holding on to gains after results news and trading 18p higher at 540-1/2p.
Dealers said thin volumes were exaggerating price moves.
